audit_scope.description: This batch covers both EL and CL logic. EL topics include transaction validation (EIP-1559, EIP-3860), EVM execution (bitwise ops, byte utils), JSON-RPC interfaces (EIP-1898, EIP-1901, EIP-3155), and wallet provider security (EIP-5593). CL topics include slashing protection interchange (EIP-3076) with beacon node interactions.

out_of_scope: Beacon Chain state transitions beyond slashing protection

threats: Invalid blocks with incorrect base fee

cl_vectors.entry_point: Beacon Node API (block signing requests, attestation requests)

cl_vectors.source: Malicious Validator Operator / Tampered Import File
cl_vectors.entry_point: Slashing protection interchange import (EIP-3076 JSON file)
threats: Craft interchange file that omits critical records to enable slashing
Cross-network import via genesis root manipulation

misclassified_entities.reason: EVM Instruction Caller is an internal component (EVM opcodes calling byte utility functions). Not an external entity — it is part of the EL execution engine.
Generic 'Calling Function' is an internal component within the execution specs. Not external to the system boundary.
EIP-5757 governance process entity. This is a meta-process for EIP standards, not a runtime external entity interacting with the Ethereum protocol.
EIP-5757 governance entity. Not a runtime external entity.
EIP-5757 governance entity. Not a runtime external entity.

In the EIP-1901 method introspection subgraph, the RPC service is the system under audit itself (the Ethereum node). It should not be modeled as external to itself. The client consuming the OpenRPC document is the external entity.

Trace Consumer receives output from the system but does not send data INTO it. It is a downstream consumer, not an external data source. The Trace Requester (who sends the request) is the correct external entity.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any unauthenticated user or application can submit transactions and state queries via the public JSON-RPC endpoint. No authentication required. Covers EXT-TX-SUBMITTER, EXT-USER, EXT-RPC-CLIENT across EIP-3860, EIP-1559, EIP-1898.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Actor via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON-RPC API (eth_sendRawTransaction with oversized initcode, resource-intensive queries)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker submitting crafted transactions to exploit DoS vectors (e.g., EIP-3860 jumpdest analysis). Unauthenticated public endpoint.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Discovery Client via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any client can call rpc.discover to enumerate available methods. Unauthenticated. Covers EXT-RPC-CLIENT and EXT-RPC-CALLER from EIP-1901.

trusted_external_entities.name: Trace Requester via Debug RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External entity requesting transaction traces. Even if behind a configuration flag, the requester is untrusted and can trigger expensive computation. DoS vector.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Validator) via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators produce blocks that must be validated by EL. Blocks may contain incorrect base fees, exceed gas limits, or include invalid transactions. No trust should be placed in block content. Covers EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER and EXT-VALIDATOR from EIP-1559.

trusted_external_entities.name: Website/DApp via Browser
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Browser window.ethereum provider injection (EIP-5593 secure context check)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Websites requesting Ethereum provider access are untrusted. Provider injection is gated by secure context checks. Covers EXT-WEBSITE, EXT-ADVERTISEMENT from EIP-5593.

trusted_external_entities.name: Developer via HTTP Localhost
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: HTTP localhost with developer mode toggle (EIP-5593)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Developer mode relaxes security to allow HTTP localhost. Still untrusted because localhost could be compromised, and dev mode may be left enabled unintentionally.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Node via Validator API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon Node Validator API (block signing requests, attestation signing requests per EIP-3076)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The beacon node communicates with the validator client over a local authenticated channel. However, a compromised beacon node could request signing of slashable messages. Content (slot, epoch, signing root) must always be validated against the slashing protection database.

trusted_external_entities.name: Previous Validator Client via Interchange File
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The interchange file originates from an external validator client. It could be tampered with, corrupted, or crafted to omit critical slashing records. Full validation of schema, genesis root, BLS keys, and signing roots is required. Covers EXT-VALIDATOR-OPERATOR and EXT-EXTERNAL-CLIENT.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: format (EIP-2718 type envelope), signature, nonce, balance check (gas_limit * max_fee_per_gas + value), initcode size <= 49152 bytes (EIP-3860), max_fee_per_gas >= base_fee_per_gas (EIP-1559).
Initcode size must be checked before expensive jumpdest analysis. Size limit of 49152 bytes (EIP-3860) and initcode gas metering (2 gas/word) must be enforced to prevent DoS.
Rate limiting should be applied. The returned OpenRPC document must accurately reflect available methods. No sensitive internal information should be leaked.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: JSON-RPC state query methods (eth_getBalance, eth_getStorageAt, eth_call per EIP-1898)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block parameter must be validated: blockNumber and blockHash cannot both be present. requireCanonical flag must be honored. Error codes -32001 (not found) and -32000 (not canonical) must be returned correctly.

Tracing must be gated behind explicit configuration flag. Resource limits must be enforced to prevent DoS via expensive trace computation. Trace endpoints should not be exposed on public-facing RPC interfaces.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P block propagation / Engine API newPayload
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full EIP-1559 block validation required: gas_limit within ±1/1024 of parent, gas_limit >= 5000, base_fee_per_gas matches calculation from parent, gas_used <= gas_limit. All transactions must have max_fee_per_gas >= base_fee_per_gas.
Secure context (HTTPS) required. Origin must be potentially trustworthy per W3C spec. Third-party iframes blocked by default. Sandbox attribute must be checked for first-party iframes.
Developer mode must be explicitly enabled by user. HTTP localhost is only allowed when dev mode is active. Default state must be disabled.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Validator API (block signing, attestation signing per EIP-3076)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All signing requests must be checked against slashing protection database. Block slot must be >= minimum previously signed slot. Attestation source/target epochs must be >= minimum. No surround voting allowed. Signing roots must be compared. Missing signing roots treated as potential conflicts (conservative).

Full validation required: JSON schema conformance, genesis_validators_root must match current network, BLS public keys must be valid, signing roots must be properly formatted. Missing signing roots must be treated as conflicts. Validator must be completely stopped during import. Duplicate public keys must be merged safely.
